competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: OpenSpec is hardening its delta model into a fail-closed one: unknown metadata fails strict validation, a blocked sync stops archive, and every task needs a done criterion. These match gzkit instincts, so they reinforce spec-delta-intent-review and are not new pressure. gzkit should take the 'dry-run shows exactly which files change' pattern for sync and init surfaces. It should reject Stores as a model, because it removes the ledger as the system of record.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Spec Kit's core is still specify/plan/tasks, but since 1.0 it is a platform of presets, extensions and org-hosted catalogs, and its community catalog now carries a governance layer in gzkit's territory: decision memory that answers which ADRs govern a PR (adrkit), one policy enforced at agent, git and CI boundaries (spec-gates), and a fail-closed spec/code/ADR citation validator (arch-governance), plus evidence, drift and red-team extensions. Each is small and none composes an append-only ledger, receipts and human attestation into one system of record, which remains gzkit's distinction; the risk is that a 143k-star distribution channel makes 'Spec Kit plus a governance bundle' the default answer piecemeal. Absorb: adrkit's `affects` field (which decisions govern this change) and arch-governance's advisory-then-blocking rollout per repo. Consider distributing gzkit through a Spec Kit catalog rather than competing with its reach.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: The main lesson is supply-chain and maintainer continuity: a 64k-star workflow tool lost its home overnight, and adopters had to judge a fork's trustworthiness. gzkit should absorb this as distribution provenance (signed or attested releases, a documented succession path) and as a radar rule that re-verifies each competitor's canonical home. GSD Core's fail-closed hardening of TDD-evidence and frontmatter gates is worth tracking as convergence toward receipt-like gates; keep rejecting autonomous wave chaining that has no attestation.

evidence.label: full-send SKILL.md
evidence.summary: Defines an unattended path from change to merged PR. It requires self-observed proof, sets a merge gate (proof covers the whole diff, required checks green, bot findings fixed or dismissed with a written reason, branch mergeable, no --admin bypass) and says the 'full send' request replaces project-file rules that would have the agent ask before testing.

evidence.label: sol-loop SKILL.md
evidence.summary: Runs a bounded loop with a reviewer on another vendor's model: 3 rounds by default, 5 for security, auth or data-loss changes. Findings carry stable ids and blocker/should/nit severity in a ledger. The skill states that a timeout, an error or the end of the budget is not approval, and it forbids substituting another model.

evidence.label: council SKILL.md
evidence.summary: Sends the work to three flagship models from different providers for read-only review, scores each round out of 10 and writes a rounds-by-delegate score table into the PR description. It says 'Do not invent' a missing score and tells the agent to resist scope creep.

evidence.label: babysit-pr SKILL.md
evidence.summary: Uses one event-driven watcher per PR (the bundled pr-wait script or T3 Code's watch_pull_request) and forbids sleep loops. It verifies each bot finding against the source and declines scope-growing fixes with a written reason.

evidence.label: T3 Code repository metadata (GitHub API)
evidence.summary: This is the author's companion harness that tstack optionally uses. It had 30,267 stars and was pushed 2026-10-26.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: tstack is a personal PR-lifecycle skill pack, not a spec or governance framework. gzkit should take three mechanisms from it: the cross-vendor review round ledger with stable finding ids and severities, the rule that a timeout or exhausted budget is not approval, and an explicit merge-gate checklist. gzkit should reject two things outright: a user's trigger phrase overriding project-canon rules ('this request replaces that rule'), and agent self-confidence standing in for human review at merge. Both contradict Gate 5 and gzkit's rule that harness instructions cannot excuse a governed stage.

discovered_candidates.name: Cloudflare security-audit skill
discovered_candidates.evidence: This MIT skill was created 2026-06-18 and shows about 47.5k stars. It runs six phases that write a deterministic coverage-ledger.json and findings.json validated against report-schema.json by zero-dependency validators; every candidate goes to a fresh verifier that 'tries to disprove it', and verdicts are confirmed, needs_validation or rejected. Per its README, it seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability-discovery harness (https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness). Source: https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill
discovered_candidates.recommended_action: Admit to secondary watch. It is the strongest current example of schema-validated, independently verified review records with a coverage ledger, and maps directly onto ADR-pool.review-receipt-taxonomy and ADR-pool.agentic-security-review. Its needs_validation verdict, which carries no severity, is a pattern gzkit lacks. (pattern: review-receipts)

discovered_candidates.name: Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM), Google
discovered_candidates.evidence: This Apache-2.0 plugin was created 2026-09-13 and shows about 1.2k stars (site https://egm.dev). Per the README, deep-context 'Elephant' sessions draft specs and 'isolated zero-context Goldfish subagents stress-test them', with skills for brainstorm, draft, a multi-stage review swarm, resolve and an AST-based drift report between specs and live code. It ships for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity and is 'not an officially supported Google product'. Source: https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model
discovered_candidates.recommended_action: Admit to primary watch. It is a major vendor's spec-driven entrant with the same human-owns-outcomes stance as gzkit's Gate 5. Its zero-context reviewer isolation and spec-to-code drift report bear on gzkit's spec-reviewer/quality-reviewer stages and on ADR-pool.spec-delta-markers. Reject its prose-only review output: route findings to receipts. (pattern: proposed: zero-context-adversarial-review (adjacent to review-receipts and spec-delta-intent-review))

discovered_candidates.name: Trail of Bits: 'The sorry state of skill distribution'
discovered_candidates.evidence: Published 2026-06-03, the post reports bypassing ClawHub's detector, Cisco's skill-scanner and all three scanners integrated into skills.sh, through newline padding, poisoned .pyc bytecode and LLM-targeted prompt injection. It concludes 'No amount of scanning or LLM analysis can reliably detect malicious content in agent skills' and recommends curated marketplaces, version pinning and control over who can update. Source: https://blog.trailofbits.com/2026/06/03/the-sorry-state-of-skill-distribution/
discovered_candidates.recommended_action: Admit to reference watch, as research rather than a product. It is primary evidence that ADR-pool.content-injection-scanning must not treat a scan as a trust gate; pinning, curated provenance and a human-reviewed sync receipt have to carry the trust decision. (pattern: injection-security)

discovered_candidates.name: SpexCode
discovered_candidates.evidence: This MIT project was created 2026-06-19 and shows about 323 stars, with frequent docs releases through 2026-10-20. It is 'a Git-backed spec tree and session manager for coding agents': each spec.md names the file or function it governs in a `code:` field, drift is computed from git on every read, and each agent session runs in its own branch and worktree. Source: https://github.com/shuxueshuxue/Spexcode
discovered_candidates.recommended_action: Watch only. It is small, but the mechanism of binding each spec node to a code symbol and deriving drift from git without stored state is a concrete witness design for ADR-pool.spec-delta-markers and for gz validate --brief-reconcile. Reject its branch-per-session model, which conflicts with gzkit's work-on-main doctrine. (pattern: spec-delta-intent-review)

discovered_candidates.name: Canny
discovered_candidates.evidence: This MIT project was created 2026-09-11 and shows about 125 stars; v0.3.0 shipped 2026-09-22. It 'hooks into Claude Code and Codex CLI, keeps a ledger of what the agent actually did, and will not let it finish on a claim'. Its rule is 'Facts go to code. Judgments go to Jev. Only facts can block', and `canny replay` reproduces verdicts from the ledger. Source: https://github.com/qkal/Canny
discovered_candidates.recommended_action: Watch only. It is too young to admit, but it is the closest small-scale analogue to gzkit's 'gate evidence must witness the action' rule (AGENTS.md DO IT RIGHT #12) and the anti-vibing mantra, implemented as a stop hook. Its facts-block, judgments-advise split and deterministic replay are worth citing in the gzkit hook design. (pattern: proposed: claim-requires-ledger-evidence (adjacent to executable-contracts))

discovered_candidates.name: brain0
discovered_candidates.evidence: This Apache-2.0 project was created 2026-07-02 and shows about 314 stars, with v0.1.0 through v0.1.3 released between 2026-07-02 and 2026-10-24. It 'passively builds a decision graph of your repository: every commit linked to the agent intents behind it, down to the single function', with drift detection, a DLP audit of what agents read and a risk score. It needs 'no hooks, no agent cooperation' and reads git plus on-disk agent transcripts. Source: https://github.com/Brain0-ai/brain0
discovered_candidates.recommended_action: Watch only. It represents the verification-and-attestation-of-AI-code category, which emerged in this window. Reject passive transcript inference as attestation, because it is reconstruction, not witness. Its function-level intent linkage could inform ADR-pool.execution-memory-graph. Agent Trace has not moved past the 0.1.0 RFC of January 2026, so the category still has no settled standard. (pattern: proposed: ai-code-provenance (related: Agent Trace RFC https://agent-trace.dev/ and git-ai https://github.com/git-ai-project/git-ai))
